nodes.text: Chapter 20: Current, Resistance, Ohm’s Law, Power, AC/DC

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn simple circuit. A battery on the left is labeled V, with a pink plus sign at its upper terminal and a blue minus sign at its lower terminal. A black wire forms a rectangular loop. Blue arrows labeled I show conventional current moving clockwise: rightward across the top, downward along the right side, and leftward across the bottom. Black arrows and repeated e⁻ labels show electrons moving in the opposite, counterclockwise direction around the loop and downward through the battery.
nodes.figure_alternative: Circuit diagram contrasting clockwise conventional current I with counterclockwise electron flow around a battery labeled V.

nodes.text: Electrical current (I) is the rate of flow of positive charge.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: I equals Q divided by delta t, which equals Q divided by t.

nodes.text: It’s direction (from DC, or direct current, voltage) is opposite the ‘flow’ of electrons: from + to −.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: The unit ampere equals coulombs per second.

nodes.text: Electric fields in a Simple Circuit (1962)

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Black-and-white photograph of a simple circuit or conductor apparatus with two leads entering from the top. Dense curved field-line patterns surround and pass through the conductor. A left callout pointing into the conductor reads, “Internal electric field: constant magnitude and parallel to the axis of the conductor.” A right callout pointing to the surrounding region reads, “External electric field: Produced by the surface charges.”
nodes.figure_alternative: Annotated photograph showing internal and external electric fields in a simple circuit.

warnings.message: The source reads “It’s direction,” where the possessive “Its direction” was likely intended; the visible wording has been preserved.
